name: Personas
description:
Personas are research-informed representations of patterns found among people relevant to a design project. They typically bring together goals, behaviours, contexts and needs into a memorable character that teams can use when discussing design decisions.

A persona is a synthesis artefact rather than a research method in itself. Its usefulness depends on the quality of the evidence and analysis from which it was constructed.
whenToUse: Use personas when substantial research has revealed meaningful patterns in goals or behaviours and a team needs a shared representation of those patterns during design.
steps: Identify recurring behavioural and goal-related patterns.
Distinguish meaningful differences from superficial demographics.
Group related patterns into coherent behavioural archetypes.
Construct a concise persona for each important pattern.
Include evidence-relevant goals, behaviours and contexts.
Communicate where the persona came from and what it does not represent.
Revisit personas as new research becomes available.
lookOutFor: Personas created from imagination can easily reproduce stereotypes.
Decorative details can make a persona memorable while adding little design value.
Do not imply that one persona represents every person within a demographic group.

resources.citation: Cooper, A. (1999). *The Inmates Are Running the Asylum*. Sams.
Pruitt, J. & Adlin, T. (2006). *The Persona Lifecycle*. Morgan Kaufmann.
